value: Williams Geismar Olefins Plant, Geismar, Louisiana; owned by Williams Olefins LLC, subsidiary of Williams Companies, Inc.
quote: Williams Olefins LLC, which owns and operates the Williams Geismar Olefins Plant.

value: Ethane and propane
quote: ethane and propane enter "cracking furnaces" where they are converted to ethylene and propylene

value: Furnace effluent gases enter heat exchangers then quench tower for further cooling by direct contact with quench water sprayed downward from top
quote: enter heat exchangers that reduce the temperature of the gases. The furnace effluent gases then enter the quench tower for further cooling by direct contact with quench water, which is sprayed downward from the top of the tower.

value: Closed-loop circulation: quench tower -> settler -> process heat exchangers (including reboilers) -> cooling water system -> back to tower
quote: quench water that directly contacts the heated furnace effluent gases is part of a closed-loop water circulation system. ... The heated quench water then serves as a heat source in various heat exchangers within the process ... Finally, a cooling water system further cools the quench water before it circulates back to the quench tower (Figure 2).

value: Removes most oily tar products that condense into quench water; some oily material remains and causes fouling
quote: The quench water settler removes most of the tar material (Figure 2); however, some oily material remains in the quench water.

value: Buildup on inside of heat exchanger tubes resulting in decrease in both heat transfer efficiency and quench water flow rate
quote: some of this material adheres to and builds up on the inside of process equipment such as heat exchanger tubes, resulting in a decrease in both heat transfer efficiency and quench water flow rate. The buildup of such material is called "fouling."

value: Evaluate quench water system by analyzing flow rates through pumps and heat exchangers to identify fouled piece causing decrease
quote: When quench water flow through the process periodically decreased due to fouling, Williams operations personnel would evaluate the quench water system by analyzing, among other things, flow rates through pumps and heat exchangers to identify the fouled piece of equipment likely causing the decrease in quench water flow.

value: Shell and tube heat exchangers
quote: The propylene fractionator Reboilers A and B are shell and tube heat exchangers

value: Tube-side hot quench water vaporizes shell-side hydrocarbon process fluid
quote: where tube-side hot quench water vaporizes shell-side hydrocarbon process fluid

value: ~95% propane with balance mostly propylene and C4s (C4 = 4-carbon molecules e.g. butane C4H10); referred to as "propane" in report
quote: approximately 95% propane with the balance composed mostly of propylene and C4s (Figure 3 and Figure 4). (This report refers to the propane mixture as "propane.")

item: Normal quench water inlet temperature to reboiler
value: approximately 185
quote: Quench water enters the propylene fractionator reboilers at approximately 185 °F

value: approximately 130
quote: partially vaporizes the shell-side propane, which enters the reboiler at a temperature of approximately 130 °F.

item: Reboiler hot quench water temperature per assignment brief
value: about 187
quote: operations supervisor opened the hot quench water (about 187 F) to its tubes

value: Both reboilers continuously operating; required periodic fractionator downtime when fouled for cleaning
quote: The original propylene fractionator design had both reboilers continuously operating. This process design required periodic propylene fractionator downtime when the reboilers fouled and required cleaning.

value: Valves installed on shell-side and tube-side piping to allow continuous operation with only one reboiler at a time; other offline but ready, isolated by new valves allowing cleaning while fractionator continues
quote: In 2001, Williams installed valves on the shell-side and tube-side reboiler piping to allow for continuous operation with only one reboiler operating at a time. The other reboiler would be offline but ready for operation (see Section 5.1), isolated from the process by the new valves.

value: Gate valves isolating reboilers from pressure relief valve at top of propylene fractionator were not part of original design and installed in 2001
quote: The valves (gate valves) isolating the reboilers from the pressure relief valve at the top of the propylene fractionator were not part of the original design, and were installed in 2001.

value: 24 feet 8 inches long end-to-end
quote: The heat exchangers are 24 feet 8 inches long end-to-end.

value: Approximately 18.5 ft long and over 5 ft diameter
quote: Each exchanger shell (the portion of the heat exchanger that holds the tube bundle) is approximately 18.5 feet long and over 5 feet in diameter.

value: 3,020 tubes, each 3/4-in diameter; if laid end-to-end >10.5 miles
quote: The tubes are each ¾-inch in diameter, and each heat exchanger contains 3,020 tubes. To put this in perspective, if one were to lay each tube from one heat exchanger end-to-end in a straight line, the tubes would span over 10.5 miles.

value: Six-pass (depicted as two-pass for simplicity in Fig.3)
quote: Depicted in Figure 3 as a two-pass heat exchanger for purposes of simplicity, the reboilers were six-pass heat exchangers.

value: 16 months on standby since maintenance in February 2012; also described as incident occurred when propylene fractionator reboiler that had been offline for 16 months catastrophically ruptured
quote: The incident occurred when a propylene fractionator reboiler that had been offline for 16 months catastrophically ruptured.

value: Quench water flow through operating Reboiler A had dropped gradually over past day (Fig.5); entire quench water circulation rate seemed impaired
quote: the quench water flow through the operating propylene fractionator reboiler (Reboiler A) had dropped gradually over the past day (Figure 5). The group then analyzed plant data and noticed the entire quench water circulation rate seemed to be impaired.

item: Time hot quench water introduced to Reboiler B
value: 8:33 am June 13, 2013 operations supervisor likely opened quench water valves on offline Reboiler B as indicated by rapid increase in quench water flow rate Fig.6
quote: at 8:33 am, the operations supervisor likely opened the quench water valves on the offline reboiler, Reboiler B, as indicated by the rapid increase in quench water flow rate shown in Figure 6.

item: Time from hot water introduction to rupture
value: Approximately three minutes later Reboiler B exploded
quote: Approximately three minutes later, Reboiler B exploded (Figure 7).

value: Propane/propylene erupted from ruptured reboiler and fractionator due to failed piping; vapor ignited creating massive fireball; piping launched ~30 ft overhead into pipe rack
quote: Propane and propylene process fluid erupted from the ruptured reboiler and from the propylene fractionator due to failed piping. The process vapor ignited, creating a massive fireball. The force of the explosion launched a portion of the propylene fractionator reboiler piping into a pipe rack approximately 30 feet overhead (Figure 8).

value: 1 operator died at scene, operations supervisor died next day; 167 personnel reported injuries (3 Williams +164 contractors); fire ~3.5 hrs; >30,000 lbs flammable HC released
quote: A Williams operator working near the propylene fractionator at the time of the explosion died at the scene. ... The fire lasted approximately 3.5 hours, and Williams reported releasing over 30,000 pounds of flammable hydrocarbons during the incident. 14 Of the 167 workers who reported injuries, three were Williams employees and 164 were contractors.

value: Plant remained down for 18 months and restarted January 2015
quote: The plant remained down for 18 months and restarted in January 2015.
